body: Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 21 provides that, for any period, payments may be made under either a childcare subsidy granted for a child or an OSCAR subsidy granted for that child, but not both.
Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 22 requires hours of childcare assistance to be calculated weekly.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 23 provides that childcare assistance is not payable for any hour of a child's participation in an approved early childhood education programme or OSCAR programme if, for that hour, another Government funding programme purchases hours of childcare and the amount provided per hour exceeds the hourly rate of childcare assistance as calculated under regulation 24. However, MSD must pay childcare subsidy for an eligible child's participation in a licensed home-based education and care service where the educator requires a top-up payment to cover the educator's hourly education and care rate.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 24 caps the hourly rate of childcare assistance at no more than the actual hourly fee payable, or averaged hourly fee payable for a periodic flat fee, excluding payments made by a person other than the applicant. If regulation 28 applies, the cap is the higher of the fee charged for keeping open the child's place and the hourly fee otherwise calculated. Regulation 24 is subject to regulation 23.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 30 provides that childcare subsidy may be paid only for a dependent child who is no older than 5 years and 28 days and is not yet attending school; or who is 5 years old, whose caregiver or guardian intends to enrol the child in a school with a cohort entry policy, and whose cohort-entry eligibility period is active until the first term or mid-term start date on or after the child's fifth birthday; or who is under 6 years old and for whom a child disability allowance is payable.
Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 31 provides that childcare subsidy is available only if payable under regulation 32, 34, or 35.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 32 makes childcare subsidy payable for an eligible child's approved early childhood education programmes for periods totalling up to 50 hours a week if the child participates, or will participate, in 1 or more approved programmes for a total of 3 or more hours a week and the caregiver activity, other-caregiver, child disability allowance, or other-child hospital or disability allowance conditions apply.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 33 lists the approved activities for which childcare subsidy is available under regulation 32. This RuleSpec slice treats engagement in an approved activity as a factual input pending full activity taxonomy encoding.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 34 makes childcare subsidy payable for up to 50 hours a week if the child participates, or will participate, in 1 or more approved early childhood education programmes for a total of 3 or more hours a week; MSD is satisfied from a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner certificate that the principal caregiver or temporary OB or UCB caregiver has a serious disability or illness and needs childcare for the child for more than 9 hours a week; and at least 1 other-caregiver or child-disability condition applies.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 35 makes childcare subsidy payable for up to 9 hours a week if the eligible child participates, or will participate, in 1 or more approved early childhood education programmes for a total of 3 or more hours a week; the principal caregiver or temporary OB or UCB caregiver is not engaged in an approved activity; and regulation 34 does not apply.
Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 36 provides that childcare subsidy is payable at the appropriate rate stated in Schedule 2, subject to regulation 24's actual-hourly-fee cap.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 38 provides that OSCAR subsidy may be paid only for a dependent child who participates, or will participate, in 1 or more OSCAR programmes for a total of 3 or more hours a week and is either at least 5 and under 14, or is 14 or older and a child for whom a child disability allowance is payable.
Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 39 provides that OSCAR subsidy is available only if payable under regulation 41 or 42.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 40 lists the approved activities for which OSCAR subsidy is available under regulation 41. This RuleSpec slice treats engagement in an approved activity as a factual input pending full activity taxonomy encoding.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 41 makes OSCAR subsidy payable for an eligible child's participation in OSCAR programmes for periods totalling up to 20 hours a week during the school term or up to 50 hours a week during the school holidays if the approved-activity, other-caregiver, child disability allowance, or other-child hospital or disability allowance conditions apply.

Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 42 makes OSCAR subsidy payable for up to 20 hours a week during the school term or up to 50 hours a week during the school holidays if the child participates, or will participate, in 1 or more OSCAR programmes for a total of 3 or more hours a week; MSD is satisfied from a medical practitioner or nurse practitioner certificate that the caregiver has a serious disability or illness and needs an OSCAR programme for the child for more than 3 hours a week; and at least 1 other-caregiver or child-disability condition applies.
Social Security Regulations 2018 regulation 44 provides that OSCAR subsidy is payable at the appropriate rate stated in Schedule 2, subject to regulation 24's actual-hourly-fee cap.

Social Security Regulations 2018 Schedule 2, as replaced on 1 April 2026, sets childcare and OSCAR subsidy rates. For a caregiver with 1 dependent child, household income less than $1,131 a week gives $6.72 per hour; $1,131 or more but less than $2,060 gives $5.36; $2,060 or more but less than $2,232 gives $3.75; $2,232 or more but less than $2,404 gives $2.09; and $2,404 or more gives Nil. For 2 dependent children, the corresponding thresholds are less than $1,301, less than $2,370, less than $2,557, less than $2,748, and $2,748 or more. For 3 or more dependent children, the corresponding thresholds are less than $1,457, less than $2,644, less than $2,868, less than $3,091, and $3,091 or more. The four positive rates are $6.72, $5.36, $3.75, and $2.09 per hour.
